articles.description: Data Scientist | Quantitative Financial Engineer | Frontier Market Intelligence
articles.contents:
About Me
I am a Data Scientist and Quantitative Financial Engineer based in Nairobi, Kenya, operating at the intersection of machine learning, quantitative finance, and frontier market intelligence. I completed an Applied Data Science programme and am commencing my MSc in Financial Engineering at WorldQuant University in April 2026.
My work is defined by rigour, systems thinking, and a commitment to building production-grade analytical frameworks — not just models, but deployable intelligence systems.
Current Research
I am currently building a Frontier Market Regime Classification Framework, with a live operational node in Baku. This project applies advanced machine learning techniques to classify macroeconomic and market regimes across frontier and emerging markets — an underserved space in quantitative research with significant alpha generation potential.
Core methods include:
Hidden Markov Models (HMM) for regime detection
Bayesian inference for uncertainty quantification
Time-series feature engineering across macroeconomic indicators
Live data pipeline with a Baku node for real-time regime signals
Selected Projects
Churn Analytics SaaS
A PostgreSQL-backed churn analytics platform incorporating retention modelling, survival analysis, and LTV estimation. Built for production deployment using Python.
Customer Lifetime Value Platform
A production-grade CLV analytics system built with SQL, Python, R, Docker, and Kubernetes — designed for enterprise-scale customer intelligence.
Bayesian Incrementality & Geo-Lift
Bayesian causal inference framework for measuring true marketing incrementality using geo-based experiments — separating signal from noise in marketing attribution.
A/B Testing & Senior Experimentation Framework
An end-to-end experimentation platform for rigorous A/B testing, designed to meet senior-level statistical standards across product and growth teams.
Funnel & Growth Analytics Platform
A FAANG-style funnel and growth analytics platform built with PostgreSQL, SQL, Python, R, Docker, and Kubernetes.
Teaching & Lecture Materials
I launched this site in 2021 as an educational resource for those beginning their journey in R and data science. Below is an example from Lecture 1, introducing the gapminder dataset — a powerful tool for understanding global development trends through visual exploration.
Lecture 1 — Exploring Global Development with Gapminder
The gapminder library in R provides clean, curated data on GDP per capita, life expectancy, and population across countries and time. It is an excellent entry point for learning data visualisation and exploratory data analysis.
The chart below plots GDP per capita against life expectancy in 1977, with bubble size representing population and colour representing continent. It raises a fundamental question in development economics: does wealth buy longevity?



Figure 1: GDP per Capita vs Life Expectancy by Continent (1977)



Discussion Questions:
Which countries demonstrate the strongest correlation between economic growth and increasing life expectancy?
Does a higher GDP per capita reliably predict greater longevity — and where does this relationship break down?

articles.title: Blog
articles.contents:
Welcome to My Blog
This is where I document my work, research, and thinking across quantitative finance, machine learning, and frontier market intelligence. Posts are written for practitioners — expect rigour, code, and real-world application.
What to Expect
Quantitative Finance & Markets
Deep dives into financial modelling, regime classification, factor research, and quantitative strategies — with a focus on frontier and emerging markets where data is sparse and alpha is real.
Frontier Market Research
Original research on macroeconomic dynamics, market microstructure, and regime behaviour across East Africa, the Caucasus, and other underserved markets in the quantitative research space.
Machine Learning
Applied ML for finance and data science — from Bayesian inference and Hidden Markov Models to production-grade pipelines and model deployment.
R & Data Science Tutorials
Practical, code-first tutorials in R and Python. Whether you are just starting out or levelling up, these posts are built around real datasets and real problems.
Career & Learning Journey
Honest reflections on the path from curiosity to professional practice — navigating an MSc in Financial Engineering, building open-source projects, and operating as a quant in East Africa.
First post coming soon. Follow along on GitHub for live project updates.

About Me
I am Moses Martin Njuguna Gikonyo, a Data Scientist and Quantitative Financial Engineer based in Nairobi, Kenya. I specialise in applied machine learning, data visualisation, and quantitative finance, with a strong foundation in both R and Python.
I completed my Applied Data Science programme and am commencing my MSc in Financial Engineering at WorldQuant University in April 2026, further deepening my expertise in quantitative methods and financial modelling.
My current work focuses on building a frontier market regime classification framework, with a live node operating in Baku — applying cutting-edge machine learning techniques to emerging and frontier market intelligence.
My Data Science Journey
I launched this site in 2021 as a resource for those beginning their journey in R and data science. What started as a personal learning log has grown into a platform reflecting years of hands-on experience across industries.
My technical toolkit includes R & R Markdown, Python, Machine Learning, and Data Visualization — applied across projects ranging from churn analytics and customer lifetime value platforms to Bayesian causal inference and A/B experimentation frameworks.
If you are new to R, explore my introductory content — built from the ground up with beginners in mind.
